absent: Complete memory layout with sizes, alignment, and padding for core lock, lease, async node, pipe state, and user range structures.
Behavior of file operation hooks for lock testing and lease setting and their error contracts.
Detailed predicates for POSIX conflict, overlap, same owner, and unlock classification beyond dispatch.
Lifetime, expiry callbacks, and manager operations for expirable and remote locks.
Accounting thresholds and user charge mechanics for pipe buffer growth and shrink.
Security mediation outcomes for file control and lock requests.
Numeric values of ABI markers and error codes.
Common dispatcher handling for non lock file control commands and duplication semantics.

findings.text: Provides insertion point for asynchronous notification state tied to an open file. Caller supplies descriptor number, file object, address of list head, and preallocated node. If list already holds node for same file, descriptor number is refreshed and existing node is returned. Otherwise new node is published and list head updated with read copy update discipline while file marked for async delivery. No allocation occurs inside; allocation failure handling lives with caller.

Ordering for async list mutation nests file private lock outside global async table lock. Per node consistency uses node read write lock taken in write mode with interrupt protection only for the update of descriptor number. Publication of new node occurs while both outer locks held, allowing concurrent readers under read copy update without additional exclusion.

System call surface for file control validates descriptor presence and rejects path only handles except for a small allowlist of descriptor and status queries. Security mediation precedes dispatch. The 64 bit variant copies user range description into kernel, delegates lock query and lock setting to dedicated helpers, and copies result back for queries, while other commands fall through to common dispatcher.

Path only descriptors permit only duplication queries, descriptor flag access, and status flag retrieval. All other control operations are refused with descriptor error before security mediation outcome is considered.

Query interface reports the first conflicting POSIX range lock for a caller supplied range. Accepts only read and write query types except for the open file description variant which uses its own command. Rejects nonzero process identifier in open file description mode, tags query as open file description owned with file as owner, tests through file operation hook when present otherwise generic tester, then translates result back to user layout with unlock indication when no conflict exists.

User range conversion anchors start from file position or current size depending on whence and rejects unknown whence. Arithmetic guards against overflow beyond maximum offset and against negative result. Positive length defines inclusive end, negative length extends backward after validation, and zero length denotes unbounded extent. Ownership defaults to current file table and thread group with POSIX marking before type validation.
Lock type validation accepts only shared, exclusive, and unlock markers; any other value fails validation without mutating the stored type.

Test path expects a clean temporary lock with no operation vectors and matching file pointer, warning on violation. Delegates to file specific hook for general query command when implemented, otherwise uses in memory scan. Deferred completion is treated as internal error and converted to input output failure.

Conflict scan for test acquires inode lock context and walks POSIX list. Absent context or empty list yields unlock result without locking. Entries whose manager reports expirability are expired outside the lock with module reference held, then scan restarts. First conflicting entry is copied into caller result; otherwise result is marked unlocked. All list mutation protection relies on the inode context lock.

Unlock queries match only entries sharing ownership with overlapping extent. Other queries defer to general POSIX conflict predicate over core attributes. This distinction allows unlock probing of same owner ranges without reporting unrelated owners.

Reporting translates internal owner identifier to caller namespace, with special handling for open file description locks, remote or nonpositive identifiers, and initial namespace shortcut under read copy update protection. Legacy 32 bit reporting validates that start and finite end fit in smaller offset range and fails on overflow, while 64 bit reporting copies directly. Zero length encodes unbounded end and whence is normalized.

Setting interface establishes or removes POSIX range locks with support for classic and open file description commands. Open file description commands require zeroed process field, remap to classic wait or nonwait variants, and reassign ownership to file with dedicated flag. Blocking variant adds sleep marker. After successful wait, a race where descriptor table no longer maps to same file triggers removal of all POSIX locks for that file table entry and descriptor error, except when unlocking or for open file description locks.

Descriptor race validation after lock acquisition holds file table lock while looking up descriptor number, ensuring ordering against close path removal of POSIX state. Read copy update alone is insufficient for this ordering.
Lock establishment requires file open mode compatible with requested type: shared requires readability and exclusive requires writability, while unlock imposes no mode requirement.

Blocking acquisition first applies security check on requested type, then repeats file lock operation while completion is deferred, sleeping interruptibly until blocked membership empties. Any interrupt aborts loop. Block bookkeeping is always released afterward, with fast path avoiding global blocked lock when blocker pointer is clear and no pending requests exist under acquire semantics, otherwise global lock protects wakeup, unlink, and release store.

Removal from wait graph serializes concurrent wakeup and unlink under global blocked lock. Blocker pointer transitions use acquire load and release store so that a clear pointer plus empty request list permits lockless early exit with not found status. Presence of blocker yields success status after wakeup and unlink.

Lease and delegation control exposes query and update operations keyed by read, write, and unlock types with zeroed flag and padding requirement. Directory targets reject lease establishment. Unlock bypasses allocation and clears state directly using file as private token; other types allocate lease plus async helper and delegate to virtual setter with cleanup of any surviving allocations.

Virtual lease setting enforces ownership or privilege, then security mediation, then file system hook dispatch. Missing file system hook yields invalid argument. Non unlock operations emit notification through shared chain before dispatch; unlock emits none. Optional caller supplied lease pointer receives notification context when present.

Lease creation uses zeroed slab cache allocation with list head initialization, followed by type validation, owner assignment to file, process group capture, file reference, flavor flags, and lease manager binding. Any failure frees the object and propagates error encoded as pointer.

Pending lease state clears downgrade marker on read downgrade request and clears both downgrade and unlock markers on unlock request, with fall through semantics. Time expiry treats zero deadline as immortal and otherwise compares current tick counter against deadline.

Pipe control multiplexes size query and size update under pipe mutex. Query reports capacity as slot count times page size. Update rounds request to power of two with page minimum and rejects oversize or zero slot outcomes, refuses changes while watch queue attached, enforces privilege and accounting limits on growth while always allowing shrink, and reverts accounting on failure. Resize rejects index overflow and shrink below occupancy with busy error, copies live buffers into fresh zeroed ring compacted at origin, updates accounting and capacity, and wakes writers.

Pipe size control holds pipe mutex across validation and mutation. Ring replacement additionally holds reader wait lock with interrupts disabled while sampling indices, checking occupancy, swapping buffer array, and updating position counters, capacity, and accounting, ensuring readers observe consistent snapshot.

Pipe helper resolves private pipe state only when file operation vector matches anonymous or first in first out pipe handlers and private pointer is present. Splice path additionally rejects pipes with attached watch queue. Builds without watch queue support report absence unconditionally.

Observed state includes core lock attributes for type, owner, process, file, flags, wait queue, and blocked linkage; range attributes for start and end with operation vectors; lease wrapper binding core to manager operations; async node carrying magic, file, descriptor, next link, and synchronization; pipe state carrying mutex, ring array with size and position indices, usage and accounting counters, user reference, wait queues, and optional watch queue; user range descriptors carrying type, whence, start, length, and process fields.

Hazards include silent truncation if 32 bit range reporting omitted overflow checks, offset arithmetic overflow without explicit guards, treating deferred test completion as success instead of error, missing descriptor race leading to stale POSIX locks after close, shrinking pipe below occupancy corrupting live data, oversized slot count exceeding position index range, and resizing or growing pipe under memory pressure or privilege bypass.

Binary interface distinguishes lock types F_RDLCK for shared and F_WRLCK for exclusive and F_UNLCK for release, query and update commands F_GETLK and F_SETLK and F_SETLKW with open file description forms F_OFD_GETLK and F_OFD_SETLK and F_OFD_SETLKW and 64 bit forms F_GETLK64 and F_SETLK64 and F_SETLKW64, origin markers SEEK_SET and SEEK_CUR and SEEK_END, pipe controls F_SETPIPE_SZ and F_GETPIPE_SZ, and internal flavors FL_POSIX and FL_OFDLCK and FL_SLEEP and FL_LEASE and FL_DELEG plus pending markers for downgrade and unlock.

Binary interface uses access markers FMODE_READ and FMODE_WRITE and FMODE_PATH, privilege markers CAP_LEASE and CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, granularity PAGE_SIZE with bounds OFFSET_MAX and OFFT_OFFSET_MAX, async markers FASYNC_MAGIC and FASYNC, deferral marker FILE_LOCK_DEFERRED, and negative errors EINVAL and EACCES and EBADF and EOVERFLOW and ENOMEM and EPERM and EBUSY and ENOLCK and ENOENT and EIO and EFAULT.
